clinicalPearls: Classical form results from deficiency of cystathionine beta-synthase, causing accumulation of homocysteine and methionine
A Marfanoid habitus with tall stature and arachnodactyly can mimic Marfan syndrome, but lens dislocation here is typically downward whereas in Marfan it is usually upward
Downward ectopia lentis, progressive myopia and glaucoma are characteristic ocular features
Thromboembolism affecting arteries and veins is the leading cause of morbidity and death and may occur at any age
Skeletal involvement includes osteoporosis, scoliosis and a Marfanoid build; intellectual disability and psychiatric disturbance are common
Around half of patients respond biochemically to pyridoxine (vitamin B6), which is a key determinant of phenotype severity and management

Management principles include a methionine-restricted diet, cysteine supplementation, pyridoxine trial, and folate and vitamin B12 cofactor support, with betaine to promote remethylation of homocysteine
Detectable on expanded newborn screening through elevated methionine, allowing early dietary intervention before irreversible damage
reference.pathophysiology: Classical homocystinuria is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by deficient cystathionine beta-synthase activity in the transsulphuration pathway. The enzyme normally condenses homocysteine with serine to form cystathionine using pyridoxal phosphate as cofactor. Its deficiency leads to accumulation of homocysteine and its precursor methionine, and reduced downstream cysteine. Elevated homocysteine damages vascular endothelium and interferes with collagen and elastin cross-linking, explaining the thrombotic tendency, lens zonule failure and connective-tissue features. Homocysteine can be partly diverted back to methionine by betaine-dependent remethylation, the basis of betaine therapy.
additionalDifferentials: Remethylation defects (e.g. MTHFR deficiency, cobalamin metabolism disorders)
Sulphite oxidase / molybdenum cofactor deficiency causing lens dislocation
Ehlers-Danlos and other heritable connective-tissue disorders
additionalInvestigations: Plasma total homocysteine (markedly elevated) and plasma amino acids showing raised methionine
Urine amino acids and homocysteine measurement
Enzyme assay of cystathionine beta-synthase in fibroblasts and molecular CBS gene testing
Pyridoxine responsiveness testing under controlled conditions
Ophthalmological assessment for ectopia lentis and DEXA for osteoporosis
redFlags: Acute arterial or venous thromboembolism, including stroke, myocardial or pulmonary events, which may be life-threatening
Perioperative period carries a high thrombotic risk requiring specific precautions
Acute visual loss from lens dislocation into the anterior chamber or acute glaucoma
Undiagnosed young patient with unexplained thrombosis and a Marfanoid appearance
reference.prognosis: Prognosis depends heavily on pyridoxine responsiveness and on early detection through newborn screening; early treatment can prevent intellectual disability, ectopia lentis and thromboembolism, whereas late or untreated disease carries substantial risk of vascular death and disability.
pitfalls: Mistaking the condition for Marfan syndrome and overlooking the treatable metabolic cause
Failing to distinguish classical CBS deficiency from remethylation defects, in which methionine is low rather than high
Not recognising and mitigating the heightened perioperative thrombotic risk
Assuming a normal newborn screen excludes the diagnosis in a symptomatic patient, since some cases are missed
management: Establish pyridoxine responsiveness and treat responders with pyridoxine, usually with folate and vitamin B12 as cofactors
In non-responders, institute a methionine-restricted diet with cysteine supplementation to lower homocysteine
Add betaine to promote remethylation of homocysteine to methionine and further reduce homocysteine
Reduce thromboembolic risk through perioperative prophylaxis, avoidance of dehydration, and antiplatelet or anticoagulant therapy as indicated
Monitor plasma total homocysteine and methionine to titrate therapy, with ophthalmology surveillance for ectopia lentis and glaucoma and bone-density assessment
Manage ocular and skeletal complications such as lens dislocation, myopia, scoliosis and osteoporosis, and provide psychiatric support
Refer to metabolic medicine and dietetics, initiating early treatment where newborn screening detects the disorder
Offer genetic counselling and family testing given autosomal recessive inheritance
